chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say, whenever the birth of a woman was imminent: 'Remove the women who are in the house, so that none of them be the first to look at the private parts.'

key_terms.عَوْرَة: That which must be covered, private parts — in fiqh, the body parts that must be concealed and whose exposure is forbidden
key_terms.نَاظِر: One who looks, a viewer — the person first to see the newborn's private parts
key_terms.وِلَادَة: Birth, delivery, childbirth — the process of giving birth

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn say about the etiquette during childbirth?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) narrates that his grandfather Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin, AS) would instruct those attending a birth to remove women from the birthing room so they would not be the first to look at the exposed private parts of the newborn or mother. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential concern for protecting modesty (hayaa') and limiting exposure of the 'awra even in a necessary medical context. In the early Islamic household, midwives and female attendants would be present at births, and this instruction regulated who should be the first to handle and view the newborn.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Al Sakuny, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Whenever a birth for a wife presented itself for Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, he used to say: ‘Exit the ones from the women out from the house, they would not be the first ones to look at privacy’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from ibn Muskan from Jabir who has said the following: “
At the time of the birth of a child, Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, ’Send all women out of the house; they must not be the first to look at the privacy [genitals].
